thread:
anya: Quick heads-up — after flipping FlashAttention-v2 as the default kernel for rtx-pool, some LLM endpoints show lower tokens/sec when KV-cache hit rate is high. Saw this on the customer repro (long context + high cache locality). Anyone else?

mike: I saw a similar blip in the nightly perf dashboard. throughput down ~18% on batch sizes 1-4 for seq_len=4096, KV hit ~80%. CPU usage up too. :thinking_face:

sam: Can you paste the perf snippet / pprof?

anya: Sure, here's one run from the repro host (trimmed):

```
$ ./perf_tool --model gpt-like --kernel flash-v2 --seq 4096 --bs 1 --kv-hit 0.8
tokens/s: 470
GPU util: 62%
smem (MB): 512
latency p50/p95: 220ms / 480ms
cost calc: (1M tokens / 470 tps) -> ~2128s => $0.18 per 1M tokens @ $0.15/hr GPU (est)
```

ania: infra-bot applied the old kernel selector yesterday during the canary, noted a fallback rule change. infra-bot: kernel-selector v1.9 deployed to rtx-pool.

infra-bot: roll event: kernel-selector v1.9 -> sticky rules for cache-heavy requests. :robot_face:

clair: Interesting that GPU util is only 62% — sounds like memory stalls or kernel serialization. Could be increased shared memory thrash or extra copies when KV is hit.

mike: I profiled with nvprof and saw more divergent warps on flash-v2 when KV hit path executed vs cold path. nvprof trace shows extra synchronization at tile boundary.

sam: Did we change the tiling size or alignment in v2? Might be causing boundary handling to run scalar path more often.

anya: Yes, v2 introduced 128->64 tile fallback for odd lengths to reduce SM occupancy variance; but that probably triggers on heavy KV reuse because cached keys append different seq offsets.

zuo: Quick suggestion: add a heuristic in selector: if kv_hit_rate > 0.6 and seq_len >= 2048 -> prefer fused/paged kernel. That got us better tokens/sec in our sim.

mike: Agreed. I ran a microbench:
```
kernel, kv_hit, seq, bs -> tokens/s
flash-v2, 0.8, 4096, 1 -> 470
flash-fused, 0.8, 4096, 1 -> 560
flash-v2, 0.1, 4096, 1 -> 820
```
So v2 is great for cold prefix but regresses for hot KV.

clair: Cost impact is real: moving traffic that hits cache back to fused reduces $/M tokens ~15% in that config. We should quantify across model sizes.

anya: Proposal: temporary selector change + quick A/B: route 10% of traffic with kv_hit>0.5 to fused for 24h and compare tokens/sec and cost. Owner: mike + zuo.

mike: I'll add the selector rule. Plan: 1) add metric for per-route tokens/sec split by kernel 2) run 24h 3) collect p50/p95 and $/M tokens computed from tokens/sec and instance-hour pricing.

sam: Also add a microbench job to nightly that simulates kv_hit distribution (0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9) and reports best kernel and cost. That'll catch regressions early.

anya: I'll owner the A/B and the repro. mike/zuo do the selector + dashboards. sam do the nightly job. clair, can you help validate the nvprof traces?

clair: Yep, I'll triangulate the heatmaps and point out the exact sync ops we can remove.

infra-bot: experiment created: exp-1902345678-kv-fallback-ab. Start 2026-03-10T16:00Z.

mike: Nice. One more note — set batcher to prefer >1 for fused fallback if possible; we get better throughput with small batching on fused.

anya: Good call. Also add a cheap dashboard card showing estimated $/M tokens per kernel so PMs can see cost delta.

sam: I'll spike the nightly microbench and upload results to the perf bucket.

anya: Thanks everyone. If we see A/B win, we'll flip selector for rtx-pool and add a canary for other pools. :thumbsup:

mike: Filed follow-up issue: PERF-4822 "kernel selector: KV-hit aware routing + nightly microbench". Assigning to @mike/@sam/@zuo.

anya: Closing loop: aim to ship selector fix and nightly by EOD Friday. Checkins to the thread please. :eyes:
